before.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

after.description: AS a Content Author, I WANT to preview draft entries in CMS, SO THAT I can see how content will be shown on the website. This requires: (1) adding live_preview configuration to the Contentstack SDK Stack initialization in src/services/contentstack.ts, (2) installing and initializing the @contentstack/live-preview-utils SDK to subscribe to draft content change events, (3) wiring Live Preview event callbacks into the ContentstackContext provider so that useContent() consumers re-render with updated draft data, and (4) configuring Custom Preview URLs in the Contentstack CMS dashboard. Limitation: protected/authenticated pages may not be previewable. The app uses Next.js Pages Router, not App Router, so the Contentstack App Router CSR guide must be adapted accordingly.
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
verificationCriteria: When a content author views a page in preview mode, the page renders draft (unpublished) content from the CMS, displaying content that has been saved but not yet published.
Protected pages and protected content are not rendered in preview mode.

notes: Novel capability — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The app uses Next.js Pages Router (src/pages/_app.tsx), NOT App Router, so the Contentstack App Router CSR guide cannot be followed literally. The contentstack SDK v3.15.2 accepts a live_preview config key. The @contentstack/live-preview-utils package is NOT installed and must be added. The ContentstackContext is a simple createContext with no provider in _app.tsx — the provider is mounted at the page level. Two attachment points: (1) the options config + Stack creation in contentstack.ts where live_preview config must be added, and (2) the context provider where Live Preview event listeners must trigger reactive re-renders for useContent() consumers. Custom Preview URLs are CMS dashboard configuration, not application code — that portion of the story is configuration work, not FE development, which partially explains the FE-only estimate contradiction.

notes: Openspec provided zero ACs but excellent technical notes. I built the full AC list from scratch, grounded in the actual code I read. Key observations from code review: (1) contentstack.ts creates Stack with a plain options object — AC-1/AC-2 cover the live_preview config addition with graceful fallback. (2) ContentstackContext is a bare createContext with no Provider or hook — the story's mention of 'useContent() consumers' likely refers to any component using useContext(ContentstackContext), so AC-4 is phrased generically around context consumers re-rendering. (3) The context has no provider component in the file; search for ContentstackContext.Provider returned zero matches, confirming the provider is mounted elsewhere (page-level). AC-4/AC-8 assume the provider will be enhanced to subscribe to LP events. (4) @contentstack/live-preview-utils is confirmed NOT in package.json. (5) AC-5 ensures SSR safety since the app uses Next.js Pages Router with SSR/SSG. (6) AC-9 addresses the stated limitation about protected pages. (7) AC-10 covers the Custom Preview URL configuration — this is partly CMS dashboard config but the app must correctly handle the preview URL with hash params. (8) AC-11 covers error handling for malformed LP data. (9) AC-12 addresses bundle impact — important because the LP utils should not bloat production for regular visitors.
